channel.title: Chokepoint
channel.description: AI chokepoint companies, numbers from filings

item.title: AeroVironment's LOCUST laser weapon wins its first overseas commercial order, worth $52 million
item.description: A foreign buyer has placed an order for a laser weapon for the first time. This shows that this type of equipment is moving toward commercial sale, not just staying in development.

item.title: One Prompt From Jensen Lets the Agent Set Itself Up
item.description: Setting up an AI assistant used to mean configuring it step by step by hand. This demo shows that the setup can be handed to AI, which is a signal for people who want to start using agents.

item.title: Compute can go live as soon as 14 days after the data center is built
item.description: Nvidia pre-builds and tests DSX POD before delivery, so AI builders can start using compute faster.

item.title: Mistral and NVIDIA Team Up to Bring AI Into Industrial Engineering Design Rooms
item.description: Engineers spend a lot of time on simulation and chip design. This partnership aims to have AI help directly, which affects the people who actually build things.

item.title: DeepSeek Processes 155 trillion tokens a Day and Earns $38 per GPU Hour
item.description: Until now, outsiders could mostly only guess whether AI services make money. DeepSeek has published its own revenue figures, so anyone can run the numbers with real data.

item.title: DeepSeek Orders 160,000 Huawei Ascend 950DT, but Delivery Could Take More Than a Year
item.description: The order is not the problem. Capacity for high-end memory and similar parts is the bottleneck, so this large order can only be delivered slowly.

item.title: $AVAV signs three MOUs in one week, but the press release has no amounts, and the stock fell about 5% on October 14
item.description: A cooperation memorandum sounds exciting, but it has no amount and no binding force, so it is still far from a real order.

item.title: $KTOS Announced Awards "More Than $100 Million," but No Matching Filing Shows Up
item.description: A number only counts toward expectations once it can be matched to official filings. Otherwise, it is just news.

item.title: $KTOS Gains One More Analyst, but Average Price Target Falls from $99.57 to $98.33
item.description: An analyst's price target shows their view of the stock, and this time more analysts issued one while the average target went down, so it is worth a closer look.
